aria: Animated recap of the Lakers' 118 to 114 overtime win over the Hornets: Quentin Grimes' tying 3-pointer with 1.7 seconds left in regulation, quarter-by-quarter scoring, his career-high 47 points and 10 threes, the top scorers, how the Lakers won, and Wednesday's game against Utah.
notes: Box score from the Lakers' 118–114 overtime win over the Charlotte Hornets at Crypto.com Arena on Nov 17, 2026, from the CBS Sports box score, checked against the Covers box score, with game details from the Associated Press (via WSLS), NBC Sports, The Sporting Tribune (via Yahoo Sports) and Lakers Nation. All 118 Los Angeles points and all 114 Charlotte points are accounted for: the CBS box score's player lines add up to 118 once Kevon Looney's 4 points (from Covers) are added, and its Charlotte lines add up to 114 with Moussa Diabaté, Naz Reid, Brandon Miller and Coby White filled in from Covers (CBS's page did not list those four). Covers lists Sandro Mamukelashvili with 5 points, which would make 120, so his CBS line (3) is used. The quarter scores add up to both totals: Charlotte 34–30 after one, 66–59 at the half, 94–81 after three, 111–111 after regulation, 7–3 Lakers in overtime. Team stats (threes 18 of 50 to 18 of 54, free throws 18 of 29 to 16 of 20, offensive rebounds 19–12, turnovers 13–18, field goals 41 of 99 to 40 of 87) are from the CBS box score; fast-break points (27–9) and the biggest leads (Charlotte 18, Lakers 4) are from Covers. Records and ranks are from the site's standings after Tuesday's games.

Charlotte led by 18 in the second half (AP; NBC Sports says late in the third after a 16–2 run). Grimes scored 21 of the Lakers' 30 in the fourth (AP; The Sporting Tribune). Charlotte went up 110–106 late; Grimes made a layup, Coby White made one of two free throws, and Dončić found Grimes for the tying three with 1.7 seconds left (AP; CBS play-by-play). Brandon Miller and Coby White sat out overtime (AP; NBC Sports). Grimes forced a turnover on a Charlotte inbounds play late in overtime and made two free throws (AP; The Sporting Tribune). His 47 points and 10 threes were career highs, and he joined Kobe Bryant as the only Lakers to make 10 threes in a game (AP; NBC Sports; Lakers Nation). It was the Lakers' ninth straight win (AP). Austin Reaves (bruised heel) and Walker Kessler (leg soreness) were out (AP). The Lakers host Utah on Wednesday (AP; Lakers Nation).

The play of the game is an original illustration of Quentin Grimes' 3-pointer with 1.7 seconds left in regulation that tied it 111–111 (AP gives 1.7 seconds and credits Dončić with the pass; the quarter scores confirm 111–111 after four, and Charlotte's 110–106 lead before Grimes' layup and White's one-of-two free throws puts the score at 111–108 before the shot). NBC Sports quotes Grimes saying he was "too open." The recaps don't describe the shot further, so it is drawn as the template's plain pull-up from beyond the arc. The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The music is an original beat made for this page. No existing recordings or melodies are used. This is an unofficial fan recap, not affiliated with the Los Angeles Lakers or the NBA, which is why it carries a plain basketball mark and the team's colors but not the team's logo.

The shooter in the play of the game is drawn to Grimes' listed 6-foot-5 and 207 pounds (Wikipedia), with his arms scaled to the 6-foot-8 wingspan measured at the 2021 NBA Draft Combine (NBADraft.net), in the Lakers' home gold with No. 5 (Wikipedia). He has no approved look on file yet, so he is drawn in the kit with the default skin tone. It is an original figure with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
